title.narrative: Strengthening rural governance for the right to adequate food Phase ii

description.narrative: Overall Objective (Impact ): Progressive governance for the right to food, guided by the principles of participation, transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and rule of law, for improved food and nutrition security in rural communities.Overall outcome :Duty bearers in the program countries (Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe) progressively enact and implement inclusive legal frameworks, policies and programs that are conducive to the realization of the right to food and that promote accountability.

The project will be implemented at National level and two districts Mangochi and Chitipa targeting a wide range of participants.On a national and district level, the following organizations, government entities are going to be directly targeted: NGOs and CBO's working in food and nutrition, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Local Government, Ministry of Trade, Mangochi district council, Parliamentary Committee on Agriculture, Parliamentary Committee on Budget, Parliamentary Committee on HIV/Aids and Nutrition, Women Caucus on Parliament, Private Sector, district CSO Networks, Malawi Human Rights Commission.At the local level, the project will be implemented in Mangochi district in the area of TA Lulanga on the far end of the Eastern bank of the South-East Arm of Lake Malawi. The area has 1 ADC and 12 Village Development Committees (VDCs). The total population for the area is 43, 1011 distributed by gender as 21,120 Males and 21,981 females. Out of these, 19,466 are youth (aged between 10 and 35) representing 45 %. 7894 of the total population is aged under five. In Chitipa the project will be implemented in TA Mwene Wenya targeting in 9 Group Village Heads .

The right to food project in Malawi envisions administrative, political and traditional duty bearers to deliver better on the right to adequate food, guided by the principles of participation, transparency and accountability, non-discrimination, and rule of law. The project aims to promote better services delivery by government through actions initiated by citizen groups to hold public officials, politicians and service providers accountable for their conduct and performance in delivering services, improving people's welfare and protecting people's rights. The project activities and interventions are being implemented at the micro (community), meso (Mangochi and Chitips district) and macro (national) levels using the Human Rights Based Approach (HRBA).
